articles.title: Design Museum Gent / Carmody Groarke + ATAMA + RE-ST
articles.summary: After four years of intensive renovation and expansion, Design Museum Gent will opened its doors close to UNESCO World Heritage sites. What was once a charming but fragmented ensemble of buildings is now a renewed, forward-looking museum that brings together history, innovation and sustainability. The transformation includes both the restoration of listed buildings dating from the 16th to the 20th century and the addition of a striking new wing that gives the museum a fresh, contemporary appearance.

Parametricism as Style, written by Patrik Schumacher , then a partner at Zaha Hadid Architects , called it "the great new style after modernism" and recast Postmodernism and Deconstructivism as "transitional episodes" that had prepared its arrival. articles.title: Student Dining Block at S. R. University / SJK Architects
articles.summary: The design of the Student Dining Block at S. R. University creates a visually light, scaled-down structure with humble proportions that deliberately belies the scale of its operations—the facility provides over 16,000 meals to 5,400 students every single day. Wide landscaped streets, amphitheatre-style stairs, and courtyards are integrated into the design, elevating the dining area into a lively communal hub that nurtures conversations and camaraderie.

The brief was practical, yet the client hoped for more: a structure that would be beautiful, meaningful and expressive of the company's identity. articles.title: Casa Sierra Morena I / Gallese Arquitectos
articles.summary: Sierra Morena House I was designed around the idea of structural honesty, allowing the structure, materials, and openings to define the architecture without relying on additional finishes, while keeping maintenance to a minimum.

articles.title: Bar Barra Peñasco / Estudio CR
articles.summary: Barra Peñasco is a high-end bar inside the Rosewood Mandarina Hotel in the Riviera Nayarit. Perched on a cliffside between the canopy of white fig trees and palms, it faces the Pacific Ocean. The project responds to the site's unique conditions through an open architecture that accompanies different moments of hospitality: arriving, taking a seat, sharing a drink, and lingering as the sunset transforms the horizon and music extends the experience into the night. Its mixology menu, inspired by the four elements and Náyeri and Wixárika traditions, dialogues with this natural setting.
